sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 22062022 at about 8.45 a.m., the Petitioner was proceeding in XL Heavy Duty bearing No.KA03HH2571 at Bandapura Gate, Service road, Avalahalli,
Bangalore.
At that time a car bearing No.KA01G5756 driven by its driver came in high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to East Point hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was running tailor shop and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/ p.m.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the car and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.
In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of car.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it contended that the accident has taken place due to negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle.
It is further contended that the rider of motor cycle had no valid driving licence and not wearing head guard as on the date of accident.

Hence,
among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 22.06.2022 at about 8.45 a.m. near Bandapura gate, Service road, Avalahalli,
Nagaraja.

2
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA01G 5756?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes.
What is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
He also examined doctor as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P15 and 16 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any evidence.
PW.1 and 2 have been cross examined at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.2.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 22062022 at about 8.45 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the car bearing No.KA01G5756.
8.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA01G5756.
9.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P14.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot Panchanama along with sketch, Police notice and Reply, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.9 is the discharge summary.
Ex . P.10
is Medical bills.
Ex. P.11
is the Prescriptions.
Ex . P.12
and 13
are Xrays and Ex.P.14 is the notarised copy of Aadhar card of PW.1.
Ex. P.15

is the outpatient record and Ex.
P.16 is the X ray.

10. Upon going through Ex.P1 and 2 i.e., FIR and Complaint which shows that on the complaint lodged before Avalahalli Police station, the SHO of the concerned Police Station has registered a case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA01G5756 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
The documents Ex.P.3 annexed with Spot sketch discloses the fact that same were drawn by the IO in the presence of panchas.

The documents Ex.P.4 and 5 discloses the fact that IO secured information regarding the driver of offending vehicle as on the date of accident and document Ex. P.5 discloses the fact that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was driven by Nagaraja.

K vs The Excise Commissioner on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181071426/
3 one Mr.Vinod Kumar S.V. who is none other than the person shown as accused in Ex. P.1 and in Ex.
P.8.
The document Ex.P.5 discloses the fact that the driver of offending vehicle possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident to drive the said vehicle.
The said document would also justify the policy in respect of the offending vehicle was in force at the time of accident with the respondent No.2.
The documents Ex.P.1 to 6 and 8 clearly establishes the fact of involvement of offending vehicle and the vehicle in which the petitioner said to have proceeding in the occurrence of accident.
The document Ex.P.6 clearly establishes the fact of damages which the vehicles involved have sustained.
The document Ex.P.7 justify the fact that the petitioner herein had sustained such injuries which are mentioned therein and same also makes it clear that the injuries are grievous in nature.

There is no dispute of the fact that after thorough investigation IO has submitted charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle as per Ex. P.8 for the offences alleged punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
There is no dispute of the fact that till date said document has remained unchallenged.
11. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Somashekar.S.A as P.W.2 and got marked OPD record and Xray at Ex. P.15 and 16.
He also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
12. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
13. Further, the Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to rebut the evidence of petitioner.
In addition to this, the IO after thorough investigation filed a charge sheet against the driver of car bearing No.KA01G5756.
The said charge sheet admittedly remained unchallenged till date.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA01 G5756 and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.
14. Issue No. 2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No.KA01G5756, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 52 years.
He has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.14 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, the year of birth of petitioner is shown as 1960.
The accident took place on 22.06.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 62 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was running tailor shop and was earning a sum of Rs.35,000/ p.m.
In this regard, admittedly he has not produced any documents to substantiate the said fact.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the Nagaraja.K vs The Excise Commissioner on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181071426/
4 guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17.

sentences.text: With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
18.
The petitioner has deposed that he has sustained following injuries.
1. Lacerated wound over left foot and medial aspect measuring about 10 x 3 cms.
Tendons exposed.
2. Type III open fracture 1st metatarsal bone left foot.
3. Left II metatarsal neck fracture.
4. Left fracture of proximal phalynx 2nd toe.
5. Left fracture shaft of proximal phalynx 3 rd metatarsal bone.
6. Fracture right 8th rib.
Further the doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
19. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
20.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 22.06.2022 and discharged on 04.07.2022.

Further,
P.W.2 Dr.Somashekara.A has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 13 days.
21. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/ under this head (@ Rs.15,500/ per month).
Nagaraja.

K vs The Excise Commissioner on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181071426/
5
IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

22. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
23. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent Rs.95,000/ towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has produced 42 medical bills at Ex.P.10 amounting to Rs.26,275/.
There is no dispute about the medical bills.

Accordingly, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.26,275/
which is rounded off to Rs.26,300/as a compensation under this head.
VI
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

24. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is unable to discharge his tailoring job as earlier to the accident,
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
25. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Somashekar as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
The doctor PW.2 has even stated that the disabilities would come in the way of avocation of the petitioner.
Further, he got marked OPD record and Xray at Ex.P.15 and 16.

He assessed total disability of left lower limb at 26% and the whole body disability at 13%.
26.
In the crossexamination PW.2 has stated that he has not personally treated the petitioner He has admitted that there are fractures on the left foot of the petitioner.
He has also admitted that petitioner has recovered to the maximum.
He has denied the suggestion that he has given higher rate of disability to the Petitioner.

27. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the age of Petitioner is 7.

With multiplier of 7, income of Rs.15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,30,200/ (Rs.15,500/ x 12 =
1,86,000/, Rs.1.86,000/x 7 x 10/100 = 1,30,200/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,30,200/ under this head.
Nagaraja.K vs The Excise Commissioner on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181071426/

6 TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
28.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 26,300/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 31,000/ laid up period 6.
Loss of Future income Rs.1,30,200/ Total Rs.2,77,500/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.2,77,500/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
29. Regarding Liability:
This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA01G5756.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of car.
The Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.

Therefore,
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
30. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.2,77,500/ along with  interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E Nagaraja.K vs The Excise Commissioner on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181071426/

With multiplier of 7, income of Rs.15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,30,200/ (Rs.15,500/ x 12 =
1,86,000/, Rs.1.86,000/x 7 x 10/100 = 1,30,200/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,30,200/ under this head.

6 TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
28.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 26,300/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 31,000/ laid up period 6.
Loss of Future income Rs.1,30,200/ Total Rs.2,77,500/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.2,77,500/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA01G5756.
The Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.

Therefore,
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
30. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.2,77,500/ along with  interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E Nagaraja.K vs The Excise Commissioner on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181071426/
7 payment and after proper identification.
